> Work through this notebook: run each chunk (click ▶). The full explanations
> and the **answers** to the "👉 Your turn" tasks are on the course website.

**The question:** the volcano told us *which* genes changed. A **heatmap** shows their
*pattern* — every top gene across every sample, in one picture.

## Setup {-}

```{r setup07, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
data_dir <- c("data", "../data", "project/data", "../project/data")
data_dir <- data_dir[dir.exists(data_dir)][1]
counts <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "gene_counts.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
meta   <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "metadata.tsv"),    show_col_types = FALSE)
de     <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "DE_biofilm_vs_planktonic_24h.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

Take the genes that changed the most, and **z-score** each one (so we compare patterns,
not absolute levels):

```{r}
top_genes <- de %>%
  filter(padj < 0.05) %>%
  slice_max(abs(log2FoldChange), n = 25) %>%
  pull(gene_id)

# expression of those genes, as a matrix, z-scored per gene across samples
mat <- counts %>%
  filter(gene_id %in% top_genes) %>%
  select(-gene_name) %>%
  column_to_rownames("gene_id") %>%
  as.matrix()

z <- t(scale(t(log2(mat + 1))))      # z-score each gene (row)

heat <- as.data.frame(z) %>%
  rownames_to_column("gene_id") %>%
  pivot_longer(-gene_id, names_to = "sample", values_to = "z") %>%
  left_join(meta, by = "sample")

# order samples by lifestyle and genes by fold change, for a tidy block pattern
heat <- heat %>%
  mutate(
    sample  = factor(sample,  levels = meta %>% arrange(lifestyle, timepoint) %>% pull(sample)),
    gene_id = factor(gene_id, levels = de %>% filter(gene_id %in% top_genes) %>%
                                        arrange(log2FoldChange) %>% pull(gene_id))
  )
```

A heatmap is just one geom — `geom_tile()`:

```{r, fig.height=6}
ggplot(heat, aes(x = sample, y = gene_id, fill = z)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "steelblue", mid = "white", high = "firebrick") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "z-score") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 7))
```

Red = higher than that gene's average, blue = lower. The biofilm and planktonic samples
should split into two clear blocks — the same story as the volcano, seen gene-by-gene.

<div class="remember">
  <strong>📌 Principle:</strong> a heatmap is just <code>geom_tile()</code> — two
  categorical axes (genes × samples) and colour for the value. Z-scoring per gene lets
  you compare <em>patterns</em> across genes on very different scales.
</div>
